:::{#exm-ipw}
#### The pseudo-population in the severity example

In the population of @exm-exchangeability-strata,
with the propensity scores of @exm-propensity-score,
the weights of @def-ipw are:

| Group | patients | weight $w_i$ | weighted count |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| treated, $L = 0$ | 120 | $1/0.2 = 5$ | 600 |
| treated, $L = 1$ | 280 | $1/0.7 \approx 1.43$ | 400 |
| untreated, $L = 0$ | 480 | $1/0.8 = 1.25$ | 600 |
| untreated, $L = 1$ | 120 | $1/0.3 \approx 3.33$ | 400 |

In the [pseudo-population](#def-pseudo-population),
each treatment group has 1000 members,
600 non-severe and 400 severe:
the same severity mix as the whole population,
so $L$ no longer predicts treatment.
The weighted means are:

$$
\ba
\Est{\E{Y(1)}}_{\text{IPW}}
&= \frac{600 \cdot 10 + 400 \cdot 20}{600 + 400}
&& \text{(IPW estimator, treated)} \\
&= \frac{6000 + 8000}{1000}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 14
&& \text{(add and divide)} \\
\Est{\E{Y(0)}}_{\text{IPW}}
&= \frac{600 \cdot 8 + 400 \cdot 18}{600 + 400}
&& \text{(IPW estimator, untreated)} \\
&= \frac{4800 + 7200}{1000}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 12
&& \text{(add and divide)}
\ea
$$

These weighted means match @exm-standardization,
as @thm-ipw-identification says they should,
and their difference recovers the ATE of 2.

:::
